scope: Corollary 7.4 (Exchange of two basis members) of the manuscript “Finite tensor savings and exact Fourier circuits” (preprints/Finite-tensor-savings-and-exact-Fourier-circuits-September-25-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 130 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e2165b9f6796f018), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 37-38. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let U = (u1, . . . , un, u∗) and V = (v1, . . . , vn, v∗) be ordered bases of the same space of linear forms, viewing each list as a column vector of its forms, and let V = KU, K = A C B d ! . 37 The exchanged lists U′ = (u1, . . . , un, v∗), V ′ = (v1, . . . , vn, u∗) are both bases if and only if d ̸= 0 and det A ̸= 0. Whenever this holds, the transitions U 7→ V and U′ 7→ V ′ have equal price. The statement applies to any chosen member of each basis after reordering them to the last positions.
